Renal failure 2026-12-01 Medium

A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.

This prospective cohort study of 400 patients with active lupus nephritis used machine learning to predict complete renal response at 12 months, drawing on predictors measured at baseline and at the 3-month treatment milestone. The key finding is that incorporating 3-month follow-up data improves early identification of patients unlikely to achieve complete renal response, supporting interpretable ML models as clinical decision aids.

Journal of Korean medical science 2026-11-16 Medium

Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis.

This study used machine learning to analyze blood plasma proteins from patients with atopic dermatitis and ulcerative colitis, two inflammatory diseases that both involve overactive Th2 immune responses but affect different tissues (skin vs. gut). The analysis identified protein biomarkers that can distinguish between the two conditions, offering insight into their distinct underlying mechanisms. These findings may help improve diagnosis and understanding of tissue-specific inflammatory pathology.

A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.

This multicenter registry study developed a deep learning model to predict mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to the ICU, using a deliberately minimal set of readily available clinical variables to enable rapid risk stratification. The work addresses a gap in AI-based mortality prediction specifically for the ICU population, where evidence has been limited. The emphasis on parsimonious inputs suggests the model is designed for practical bedside deployment rather than research-only use.

Cancer science 2026-11-16 Medium

MARiO: Predicting Cancer Variant Pathogenicity by Integrating In Silico Evaluation and Patient-Level Mutational Contexts.

MARiO is a machine-learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense cancer variants by combining variant-level in silico features with patient-level mutational context from comprehensive genomic profiling. This addresses a key limitation of existing tools, which typically ignore clinical context and struggle with variants lacking established consensus. The approach aims to improve variant interpretation for precision oncology.

Deep-Learning Analysis of Peripheral Blood Smear for Prediction of Acute Inflammatory States and Chronic Comorbidities: Development and Internal Validation Study.

This study uses deep learning to analyze peripheral blood smear images and predict acute inflammatory states and chronic comorbidities. It demonstrates that morphological features of immune cells captured in routine blood smears carry predictive signal for systemic conditions, extending the utility of a standard clinical test beyond traditional manual review.

Cell 2026-11-12 High

Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia.

This study presents a single-cell multi-omic atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight human basal ganglia regions, revealing cell-type- and region-specific regulatory landscapes. It identifies candidate cis-regulatory elements and gene regulatory networks, highlighting combinatorial homeobox transcription factor expression in defining cell identity. The atlas provides a resource for understanding basal ganglia function and dysfunction in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.

This study integrates single-cell and bulk multi-omics data to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying C16orf74 as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The authors show that C16orf74 expression is associated with EMT-associated malignant states and has prognostic relevance, suggesting it could serve as a clinically accessible biomarker in HNSCC.

Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) 2026-11-10 Medium

EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.

EZpred is a deep learning method that improves enzyme function prediction (EC number assignment) by incorporating features from unlabeled sequence homologs, analogous to how AlphaFold uses homologous sequences to improve structure prediction. Unlike prior models that rely mainly on single-sequence features or labeled homologs, EZpred leverages the wealth of unlabeled homolog data to boost accuracy. This demonstrates that homolog-aware feature extraction can meaningfully advance functional annotation beyond structure prediction.

Molecular biomedicine 2026-11-09 Medium

Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.

This multicenter study developed a stacked machine-learning model combining cfDNA fragmentomic features (fragment size, nucleosome footprints, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns) from low-pass whole-genome sequencing with serum biomarkers to distinguish malignant from benign ovarian masses preoperatively. The approach was evaluated across training, internal and external test sets, and two exploratory cohorts totaling 743 participants, targeting cases where conventional serum biomarkers are uninformative.

Inflammatory bowel diseases 2026-11-09 Medium

Interpretable machine learning applied to high-dimensional salivary proteomics in pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases.

This proof-of-concept study applies interpretable machine learning to high-dimensional salivary proteomics to identify a minimal protein signature that can classify pediatric inflammatory bowel disease subtypes (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and IBD-unclassified). The approach aims to provide a non-invasive, cost-effective alternative to current invasive and expensive diagnostic methods, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and better longitudinal monitoring in children.

Journal of chemical information and modeling 2026-11-09 Medium

FlexENN: A Graph Neural Network for Binding Energy Prediction of Globular and Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.

FlexENN is a graph neural network framework that predicts binding energies for protein complexes, with separate models for folded complexes (FlexENN-F) and complexes involving intrinsically disordered proteins (FlexENN-I). It builds local interface graphs to capture interaction details, addressing the challenge that disordered interfaces often lack defined geometry. This extends binding energy prediction to a class of complexes poorly served by methods designed for folded proteins.

Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation.

This review surveys the current evidence for AI applications in obstetrics and prenatal medicine, covering prenatal ultrasound, fetal echocardiography, fetal MRI, genomic screening, risk prediction, and clinical decision support. It emphasizes the state of clinical validation and the practical requirements for implementing these tools in prenatal care.

Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.

The authors present a new method that combines graph theory and machine learning to estimate the growth rate of SARS-CoV-2 lineages from genetic sequence data. By representing distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians, they extract features that identify lineages undergoing rapid population growth. This enables real-time monitoring of large viral genomic datasets to flag emerging lineages of concern.

Metabolic Profiling Combined With Machine Learning for Assessing Clonal Hematopoiesis Status in Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: An Exploratory Analysis.

This study profiled clonal hematopoiesis (CH) mutations in a large cohort of 1817 chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) patients, finding CH in 10.8% with DNMT3A most commonly mutated. Using untargeted plasma metabolomics in 539 patients, the authors identified metabolic signatures distinguishing ITP patients with versus without CH and applied machine learning to build a predictive model for CH status. The work suggests that plasma metabolic profiles may serve as a non-invasive proxy for detecting CH in ITP.

Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.

This single-center observational study of 572 older adults compared seven classification models for identifying persistent atrial fibrillation and selected a gradient boosting machine classifier as the best performer. The work also examined clinical correlates of persistent AF in this population and interpreted the chosen model's predictors. It is a clinical modeling study with limited generalizability due to its single-center design.

Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.

This scoping review maps the literature (2021–2026) on computational methods for discovering plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening 5062 records down to 79 charted sources. It characterizes the composition of the field—mostly primary studies, with a smaller share of tools/databases—and assesses reporting practices, revealing gaps in standardization. The work provides a structured overview of an emerging computational discovery area rather than new experimental findings.

Integrating large-scale serum baseline metabolomics and APOE ε4 genotype status for the non-invasive detection of Alzheimer's disease in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort.

This study tested whether a large panel of serum metabolites, combined with APOE ε4 genotype status, could distinguish Alzheimer's disease patients from cognitively normal individuals in the ADNI cohort. The authors evaluated the discriminative performance of this combined blood-based signature as a non-invasive alternative to costly or invasive diagnostic procedures. The work supports further exploration of metabolomics-plus-genotype panels for AD stratification.

SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling.

SeqBattNet is a physics-informed neural network for battery modeling that uses a discrete-state formulation to predict remaining discharge time and energy, addressing limitations of prior PINNs that require many physical parameters or continuous state regeneration. The model also incorporates aging adaptation, allowing it to account for battery degradation over time. The work targets battery management systems but is not a biological or biomedical contribution.

Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer's Disease.

This study uses multi-omics Mendelian randomization to test whether gut microbiota, immune, and metabolic traits causally influence Alzheimer's disease, and identifies DDX17 as a potential host mediator connecting these peripheral factors to neurodegeneration. The work nominates a specific molecular target for the microbiota-immune-metabolism axis in AD, though the evidence is genetic-instrument based and requires experimental validation.

A multisource clinical deep learning model for early identification of mental disorders in first-visit psychiatric patients.

This study developed a deep learning model (TUCH-FT) to classify multiple mental disorders in 5,802 first-visit psychiatric patients using demographics, clinical history, and item-level Symptom Checklist-90 data, with final diagnoses confirmed through longitudinal follow-up and expert evaluation. The model modifies the FT-Transformer architecture to better handle heterogeneous clinical data sources, aiming to support early identification when symptoms overlap. It represents a clinical application of deep learning for multi-label psychiatric diagnosis.
